source.section: PA-40 lines 1a to 12 (form pages 1-2); PDF page 1 and form line 12 rate 3.07 percent; PDF page 9 no standard deduction or exemptions; PDF page 20 Lines 9 and 10; PDF page 21 Lines 11 and 12; PA-40 Filing Status ovals S, J, M

worked: PA has no head of household status: the form prints Single, Joint and Separate, all at one rate. Federal AGI = wages person 0 55,000.00 = 55,000.00. Federal taxable income = 55,000.00 - standard deduction 23,625.00 = 31,375.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Pennsylvania, as the projection works it: start federal AGI 55,000.00; income after reliefs = 55,000.00. No standard deduction or exemption (PDF page 9), no Line 10 deduction: state taxable income 55,000.00. Tax = 55,000.00 x 0.0307 = 1,688.50. No credit in the projection; state income tax 1,688.50. Form: Line 1a/1c 55,000.00; Line 2 0.00; Line 3 0.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 9 55,000.00; Line 10 0.00; Line 11 55,000.00; Line 12 1,688.50 (the form, in whole dollars, PDF page 4, shows 1,689). Schedule SP: Eligibility Income 55,000.00 is over 8,750.00, so no Tax Forgiveness on the form either.
accepted_approximations: Pennsylvania has no federal starting point: it adds the positive amounts of eight classes (compensation, interest, dividends, business, gains, rents, estates and trusts, gambling). The mapping runs from federal AGI to those classes: start from federal AGI, then take out what the reliefs below exempt. Wages, interest, dividends, gains, business income and rents are taken as federal AGI holds them, in one sum. The differences that remain are listed one by one in the next four entries.
